question: Two retailers, Kim and David, track sales. Kim started with 188 units. She added 32 new products. Then 119 were sold. The remaining was multiplied by 9. Then multiplied by 6 more for a monthly forecast. David had fewer items (56 units, not counted). What was Kim's final inventory?

A storage facility had 166 items. This was multiplied by 8 for a project estimate. Then divided by 4 for batch allocation. Then multiplied by 5. From this, 874 were removed for distribution. Then 10 were added from recovery. This total was multiplied by 4 again for a weekly calculation. From morning to evening, how many items remained?

A manager tracked 221 tasks. In the morning, 188 were completed. The remaining was multiplied by 3 for a follow-up estimate. Then 4 were removed for deferral. The updated amount was multiplied by 4 for a project scope. Then 25 were added as urgent items. From start to end of the day, what was the task total?

Two students, Alex and Maya, track progress. Alex started with 12 assignments. He completed 11. He added 64 more from a new unit. He multiplied by 5 for chapters covered. Then multiplied by 9 again. He added 42 study hours as extra credit. A bonus assignment worth 15 hours (not included). How many total did Alex accomplish?

A student had 114 math problems. They removed 46 as review. Then removed 1 as duplicate. They added 36 new problems. Then removed 4 for later study. These were multiplied by 4 for a final worksheet. A bonus section had 22 problems (not counted). What was the final problem count?

A storage facility had 235 boxes. It added 34 in the morning, 45 at midday, and 18 in the afternoon. Then 141 were shipped. The remaining was multiplied by 3. Then multiplied by 9 for inventory conversion. A competing facility had 67 boxes (not relevant). What was the final box count?

Two colleagues, Alex and Jamie, track productivity. Alex had 234 items. He removed 210 for immediate processing. The remaining was multiplied by 8 for verification. He added 18 more items. Then 58 were included from another batch. This total was multiplied by 7 for a final count. By comparison with Jamie's smaller total, how many items did Alex end with?

A librarian had 70 books to catalog. Morning cataloging added 6. Afternoon brought 71 more. Evening brought 18 additional books. Before closing, 46 were shelved. Two other sections had 34 books each (not counted). How many books remained to catalog?

Two project managers, Pat and Alex, track workload. Pat started with 217 items. This was multiplied by 7. Then multiplied by 4. He added 79. Then added 56 more. Then added 27 for urgent items. This total was reduced by 5230 for distribution. A colleague had 88 items. What was Pat's final workload?

A factory had 223 units in stock. This was multiplied by 8 for a production run. Then multiplied by 3. Then multiplied by 5. Then multiplied by 5 again. From this massive total, 97710 units were subtracted for distribution. A competitor had 145 units (not relevant). What was the final inventory?

Two business partners, Lee and Chris, track sales. Lee started with 113 units. This was multiplied by 5. Then 289 were sold. The remainder was multiplied by 7. Then multiplied by 7 again for a quarterly projection. Chris has fewer items. What was Lee's final total?

A project manager tracked 215 tasks. Morning removed 16. Afternoon removed 30. Evening added 7. The net total was divided by 4 for team assignment. Two other managers had 44 and 56 tasks (not included). What was the final task allocation?

A production facility had 216 units. This was multiplied by 3 for an order. He added 20 more. He added 59 from another supplier. The total was reduced by 725 (for quality control). The remaining was multiplied by 4 for packaging purposes. What was the final product count?

A coordinator had 136 volunteers. She multiplied by 6 for group assignments. Then removed 491 (counting duplicates). The remainder was divided by 5. She added 67 for late arrivals. Two other events had 45 and 78 volunteers. What was her final volunteer count?

A warehouse started with 195 items. She added 58. This total was multiplied by 6. Then 823 were shipped. She added 35 back. Finally, 401 were removed for reordering. Throughout the day, how many items remained?
A warehouse had 140 boxes. She added 8 from a delivery. Then removed 78 for shipping. Then removed 1 more. She removed 19 for restocking. By time of day (measured in hours), how many boxes remained?

Two managers, Lisa and Tom, track items. Lisa started with 197 units. She removed 60. She added 28. This was divided by 5 for group assignment. She removed 32 from another batch. She added 35 more. Tom has fewer items. What was Lisa's final count?

A student had 98 problems. She added 67 for homework. This was divided by 3 for worksheets. She added 19 more. This total was multiplied by 9 for a semester calculation. From morning until night, how many problems did she have?

A workshop started with 28 materials. He removed 8 as defective. Then removed 1 more. The remaining was multiplied by 8. Then multiplied by 4. He added 48 for restocking. Throughout the day, how many materials did he have?

Two delivery drivers, Jake and Sofia, track packages. Sofia started with 82 packages. She added 16 from a pickup. Then added 67 more. This total was multiplied by 9 for route organization. This was divided by 3 for equal stops. Then 351 were delivered. The remainder was multiplied by 7. By time of delivery (hours), what was Sofia's final count?

Two students, Ben and Maya, compare notes. Ben had 125 pages. He added 64. Then added 46. He removed 94 for a rewrite. This was multiplied by 8 for chapters. Emma had only 58 pages. What was Ben's final page count?

A warehouse had 54 boxes. He multiplied by 6 for inventory. He removed 225 for shipment. He added 37 back from a return. He removed 52 for another order. The final was multiplied by 7 for a quarterly report. A competitor had 43 boxes. What was the final count?

A distribution center had 172 packages. He multiplied by 8 for batch processing. Then multiplied by 9. Then multiplied by 7 for volume. Then 39247 were subtracted for distribution (first wave). Then 15261 more were subtracted (second wave). He added 21. A backup facility had 84 packages (not counted). What was the final count?

Two team leads, Dana and Kevin, track tasks. Kevin started with 47 items. He added 60. He removed 2. This was multiplied by 6. Then multiplied by 2. He added 66. Dana has fewer tasks. What was Kevin's final task count?

A warehouse had 76 items. This was multiplied by 9. Then 538 were removed. Then 82 more were removed. He added 49. This was multiplied by 4 for a monthly projection. Measured in time units (hours per item), what was the final total?
